speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: Moved the Appropriation Bill (No. 3) 2014-2015 seeking just under $1.4 billion in additional funding, including nearly $558 million for the Department of Defence's overseas operations and just over $115 million for the Department of Employment to meet increased job placement payments.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: Moved the Appropriation Bill (No. 4) 2014-2015 seeking just under $241 million, including $90 million for drought recovery concessional loans in Queensland and New South Wales, just over $40 million for a temporary embassy in Ukraine, and just under $35 million for additional counter-terrorism activities.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Reported that additional appropriation bills worth $1.7 billion reflect a mid-year budget update showing a $44 billion blow-out in the deficit, equivalent to $202 million a day, noted unemployment had risen to 6.4 per cent from 5.7 per cent at the last election, and said the bills incorporate a total $11.3 billion cut to foreign aid.

speeches.speaker: Eric Hutchinson
speeches.brief: Reported on infrastructure investment in Tasmania, including $400 million from the Commonwealth for the Midland Highway upgrade and a $38 million commitment to extend the runway at Hobart international airport, and said a 24 per cent tariff cut under the China free trade agreement helped a local exporter increase cherry exports from five tonnes to 190 tonnes in a year.

speeches.speaker: Rowan Ramsey
speeches.brief: Argued that federally assisted projects in Grey included airport terminal works, aged-care developments, a Coober Pedy pipeline and a Port Augusta sports hub, while warning that Australia must control borrowing to avoid the economic problems of European countries.

speeches.speaker: Terri Butler
speeches.brief: Argued the government abandoned its Paid Parental Leave scheme only to save the Prime Minister's job, citing a $16.4 billion blowout in the 2014-15 deficit revealed by MYEFO, unemployment at 6.4 per cent, and pension indexation cuts estimated to cost pensioners $80 a week.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Argued that Labor's criticism of debt and deficit is hypocritical, reporting the government is currently borrowing over $100 million more every day than it raises in tax revenue, and rejected comparisons with Greece, Spain or Portugal as complacent.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Accused the government of abandoning proper cost-benefit analysis, citing a benefit-cost ratio of just 0.45 for the East West Link compared with more than 5 for the Managed Motorways project it defunded, and said the Infrastructure Australia coordinator position had remained vacant for more than a year while listing dozens of projects re-announced despite being funded under the previous government.

speeches.speaker: Mark Coulton
speeches.brief: Welcomed restored funding for the Great Artesian Basin Sustainability Initiative, reported over 4,500 farm households in his electorate are now receiving drought support after less than 14 inches of rain in three years, and highlighted the $1 billion National Stronger Regions Fund and a $100 million mobile blackspot program for regional Australia.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Argued that the $1.7 billion appropriation bills reflect an unfair budget that hits vulnerable households, students and pensioners hardest, quoting Ben Chifley's light on the hill speech, and reported unemployment has risen to 6.4 per cent from 5.7 per cent when Labor left office.

speeches.speaker: Scott Buchholz
speeches.brief: Defended the government's economic record, citing 213,900 new jobs created last year, equivalent to 585 a day, and a Dun and Bradstreet survey finding the employment outlook the most positive in 10 years, and announced $90 million in additional drought concessional loans on top of the $280 million already committed under the 2014-15 drought package.

speeches.speaker: Nick Champion
speeches.brief: Argued a return to a Labor government would restore fairness, describing the debate on the appropriation bills as ultimately a debate on a budget of broken promises, and pointed to the Liberal Party's election manifesto full of commitments it broke.

speeches.speaker: Nola Marino
speeches.brief: Welcomed the government's continued support for the Rural Financial Counselling Service, describing its impartial support for farming families in financial crisis, and said Western Australia's service had helped over 1,000 farming businesses without a single suicide among a farmer or family member, a result a 2012 PricewaterhouseCoopers audit rated as better practice.

speeches.speaker: Keith Pitt
speeches.brief: Reported on priorities for the Hinkler electorate including a $476 million Industry Skills Fund, welcomed a Knauf Australia manufacturing plant at the Bundaberg Port worth between $70 million and $100 million expected to create 65 permanent jobs, and criticised the cost of administering the Renewable Energy Target and Renewable Energy Certificates scheme at $513 million.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Nikolic
speeches.brief: Reported progress in Tasmania, including lower unemployment, construction growth, irrigation projects, transport and airport investment, research funding, health initiatives and tourism infrastructure, and argued that coalition policies were supporting jobs, economic diversification and regional development.

speeches.speaker: Ann Sudmalis
speeches.brief: Reported government and state investment in Gilmore's roads, bridges, defence facilities, Anzac commemorations and local projects, and argued that the closure of the Shoalhaven paper mill and uncertainty over frozen-berry labelling showed the need for further employment support and clearer product information.

speeches.speaker: Fiona Scott
speeches.brief: Reported economic and infrastructure opportunities in Western Sydney, including the Sydney Science Park, medical research, transport projects and free-trade links, and described Green Army projects intended to protect Cumberland Plain bushland while supporting Indigenous employment.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: Argued that the government's budget strategy was failing, citing additional appropriations, rising unemployment, cuts to services and its debt narrative, while presenting stronger economic growth and productivity figures and supporting an amendment condemning the government's approach.

speeches.speaker: Steve Irons
speeches.brief: Supported the appropriation bills, highlighting $558 million for overseas operations, infrastructure and river projects, and funding for border protection and counter-terrorism, while arguing that government policies should be sustainable and funded responsibly.

speeches.speaker: Lisa Chesters
speeches.brief: Argued that the appropriation bills exposed a contradiction between claimed budget savings and a $44 billion deficit blow-out, while criticising cuts affecting pensions, foreign aid, public broadcasting, health, emergency management, local government and community assistance.

speeches.speaker: Ian Goodenough
speeches.brief: Supported approximately $1.74 billion in additional appropriations and highlighted the Emissions Reduction Fund, including $2.55 billion in funding, as a mechanism to support emissions reductions, energy efficiency and projects such as hydrocarbon refrigeration.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: Supported the appropriation bills as part of a necessary budget repair process, arguing that Australia's net debt to GDP of around 15 per cent required action to place the budget on a sustainable financial footing for future generations.

speeches.speaker: Ken Wyatt
speeches.brief: Discussed Appropriation Bill No. 3, which authorises about $1.74 billion in additional 2014 to 2015 spending, and detailed unmet funding needs in the Hasluck electorate for men's sheds, aged care places, and sporting facilities including the Perth Heat baseball club.

speeches.speaker: Sharman Stone
speeches.brief: Criticised the state-owned Goulburn-Murray Water as grossly inefficient compared with the irrigator-owned Murray Irrigation Ltd, noting it employs 757 staff to deliver double what Murray Irrigation manages with 136, and warned that the temporary water price per megalitre has risen from $20 three years ago to $140 this year, driving irrigators out of business.
